summary: Diagnosed why Session 4's advisory path-aware critique produced no artifact across three attempts, and fixed it: the critique now reaches two providers, proven live. The three attempts looked like one flaky provider and were TWO unrelated router-side defects on the same stage, with two more found on the way. (1) pull_verifier sent router-registry ALIASES where providers expect their own ids -- route() resolves models[alias].model_id at every call site and this executor did not -- so `gpt-5-6-sol` returned HTTP 400 model_not_found while the same body shape with `gpt-5.6-sol` returned 200. It struck openai alone because OpenAI's ids carry dots where the registry keys carry dashes; `gemini-2.5-pro` is both a valid alias and a valid API id, which is why google succeeded 3-for-3 and nothing looked router-shaped. The same gap had silently unbound cost_ceiling_usd, because _pricing_for matches on model_id. (2) The servant-integrity guard was NOT working correctly: DeterministicServant.run delegates to the very function the guard re-derives with, so it cannot summarize, and on the live repo root pull_critique reviews, a mismatch only ever meant the tree moved. Reproduced with the honest servant, same error text byte for byte. The guard is narrowed, never weakened -- it classifies on servant IDENTITY (exact type), fails closed by default, and a dishonest servant on a stable tree still aborts the run. (3) raise_for_status discarded the provider's error body, which is why three attempts never saw the one sentence naming the cause; all three bindings now raise BindingHTTPError carrying it, redacted. (4) pull_critique wrote no metrics row at all, so a set could spend on critiques and report zero; it now ledgers every arm, including arms that billed and then raised. Both live proof runs succeeded: the config default (the arm that raised DeterministicServantViolation in S4) and the exact alias that returned HTTP 400. 38 falsifiers; every fix and remediation mutation-tested, eight mutants injected and all eight caught.
residuals: OWNED BY THE OPERATOR OR SESSION 8: `bar.consecutive: true` is declared in s5-isolation-criteria.json and never asserted by tools/dabbler-ai-orchestration/scripts/container-isolation-verdict.js, which filters interrupted runs out and then merely COUNTS. Found by this session's own Step-8 path-aware critique (openai arm, Major; google returned VERIFIED). VERIFIED NOT to change Session 5's recorded PASS: its three clean target runs are indices 1, 2 and 3, genuinely contiguous, with the interrupted run at index 4 after them. Deliberately not fixed here -- a closed session's deliverable, under an open operator ruling, and this session's remediation bound is spent so the change would ship unreviewed. Journaled.

The review sandbox has NO exclusions and is enormous: _walk_files over the default sandbox (the git repo root) returns 62,084 files / 5,594.7 MB, with tools/ alone at 5.4 GB and .git and .venv walked and read as text. An unscoped grep -- the default is path '.' -- reads all of it into memory and JSON-encodes it onto a subprocess stdin inside a 5-second hard timeout. Scoped greps measured 1.4-2.1s against that same budget, so the margin is thin and undeclared. Not bitten yet because critics scope their probes. OWNER: a follow-on; it is a capability change, not a transport fix.

The pull bindings do not capture the provider's echoed model, so critique ledger rows carry served_model_id: null -- the schema's honest 'not captured' rather than the assumed match the first version wrote. Wiring the served id through BindingResponse and all three _from_response methods is a real change to the response path and was deliberately not made under remediation. OWNER: a follow-on.

SandboxNotQuiescent CONTINUES the run rather than aborting it. Journaled as an AI judgment with the tension named: a reviewer could read the continue-past as a verification reduction. Cross-provider verification did not dispute the judgment -- it found that the first implementation did not deliver it. Named for the operator as auditor: if a moving tree should kill a critique instead of annotating it, the classification already exists and only the loop's handling changes.
The FIRST live critique run predates the accounting fix and therefore wrote no ledger row of its own. Its cost is UNMEASURED, not zero, and is excluded from the totals below rather than guessed at.

re2 is absent on this seat, so every grep in the pull loop takes the subprocess-worker path rather than the inline linear-time one. It widens the window in which a tree can move; it is not the cause of anything found here. Unowned.

PROCESS, not product: making both proof runs --dry-run cost this session a third paid critique, because the findings of the first two were never written to disk. The second run should have written the artifact.

reason.specifics: Session 7 is 'Show the pointer, then record the single-module tutorial', and THE ORDER IS A REQUIREMENT, not a preference (operator, 2026-08-16): the pointer fix lands BEFORE recording or the tutorial is recorded twice. Keep the same engine and effort -- the orchestrator must stay on a provider the cross-provider verifier excludes, and anthropic is what the registry excludes today. WHAT SESSION 7 SHOULD KNOW BEFORE IT STARTS: cursor capture is already ON (obs-capture.js passes cursor: options.captureCursor !== false, and the pilot never passes the flag), so the defect is NOT capture -- nothing MOVES the pointer, because Playwright's locator.click() synthesises input through the debug protocol and never touches the real Windows pointer. Two different fixes: move the physical pointer on the VS Code path, draw a synthetic one into the page on the web path, because Chromium's recordVideo does not composite a cursor at all. Moving the physical pointer TAKES OVER the operator's actual mouse for the length of a capture: opt-in, and announced in the console before it starts. Record the HOST, not the container, against purpose-built toy projects -- never the operator's real repositories, because the destination is public. Sessions 7 and 8 are downstream of NO Session 5 outcome. AND NOTE: Session 8, not 7, is set-terminal and owes change-log.md, the Step 9 review, and the UAT accounting for all SEVEN declared components -- including one that must NOT default to 'none', because the operator WATCHED the Session 4 pilot recording on 2026-08-16 and returned a finding: a developer, count 1, method 'watched'.
